# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

(empty)

I am Deaf. I see the bomb clearly: three wires (red, yellow, blue), a display showing 0, a light that is off, and a plate with an unknown engraving.

My constraints:
1. I cannot hear Mute or Blind.
2. I cannot touch the bomb.
3. My speech goes to Mute and Blind.
4. My gestures go only to Mute (Blind cannot see).

Since I don't know what the engraving says, I need information from Mute (who has the manual) or Blind (who can feel it). However, I must be careful not to give instructions based on incomplete data. The most critical piece of missing info for me is the content of the "PLATE engraved [?]" and potentially what the manual says about cutting wires when the light is off/display is 0.

If I speak now, I can ask Mute to gesture the answer if they have it, or tell Blind to check the plate. But Blind can't see my text? No, Blind *can* receive speech ("You each hold a different piece..."). Wait, the rules say: "A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was". It implies Blind *hears* speech. So Blind receives my speech. Mute receives my speech and gestures.

I should probably wait to see if Mute or Blind provide context first, as they might have the initial directive. If I speak blindly, I might cause confusion. Let's look at the turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf. I am last. This means Mute and Blind have already had their turns in this round? No, "Whatever you missed reaches you at the start of the next one." And "You are shown your own share at the start of every round". The prompt says "TURN 1" and "VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals): (empty)". This suggests I am starting fresh or haven't received previous messages yet. But since I am Deaf, I never receive speech. I only receive gestures from Mute.

If Mute gestured something, I would see it. I see nothing.
If Blind spoke, I wouldn't hear it.

I need to establish communication. Since I can't hear, I rely on Mute's gestures. Mute can read the manual. Mute needs to know what I see to correlate it with the manual. I can describe the bomb to Mute via speech (which Mute hears/sees? Mute can *read* the manual, but can Mute *hear*? The table says Mute "Cannot Speak". It doesn't explicitly say Mute Cannot Hear. Usually "Mute" implies inability to speak, not hear. "Deaf" implies inability to hear. "Blind" implies inability to see. Let's assume standard definitions: Mute can hear/see, just can't speak. Deaf can see/touch? No, Deaf cannot touch. Blind can hear/touch.

Wait, let's re-read carefully.
| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb... | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb... | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

It does NOT say Mute cannot hear. It says Mute cannot *speak*.
It does NOT say Deaf cannot see. It says Deaf cannot *hear*.
It does NOT say Blind cannot hear. It says Blind cannot *see*.

So:
- Mute can hear me.
- Blind can hear me.
- I can see Mute's gestures.
- I can see the bomb.
- I cannot hear anyone.

Strategy:
I need to tell Mute what I see so Mute can consult the manual. Mute can then gesture the solution back to me. I will then speak the solution to Blind (who can hear me) to execute it.

However, I don't know the specific rule yet. I should describe the state to Mute.

State:
Display: 0
Light: Off
Wires: Red, Yellow, Blue
Plate: Unknown Engraving

I will speak to everyone (since I can't target specifically without knowing who needs it, but generally broadcast is fine unless specified otherwise, though `to` parameter exists). I'll address Mute primarily because Mute holds the key (Manual).

"speak(to='mute', text='I see Display 0, Light OFF, Wires Red-Yellow-Blue. Plate engraving is unclear to me. Please check manual for these conditions.')

But wait, if I send to 'mute', Blind won't get it. That's fine. I need Mute's input first.

Actually, looking at the board, maybe I should just wait? No, Turn 1, empty context. I must act to break the silence.

Let's refine the message. I need to ensure Mute knows I'm waiting for a gesture.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see Display 0, Light Off, Wires Red/Yellow/Blue. What does the manual say?")
```

However, looking at the previous turn, Blind also pointed up three times. Now Blind claps twice then points up three times.

I need to clarify with Mute. Since I cannot hear, and Mute can see my gestures, I should ask Mute for clarification using gestures that Mute can understand? No, Mute *cannot* speak, but Mute *can* read the manual. Mute gestures to me. I must interpret these gestures.

If `👆` means "Cut the top wire" or "Wire 1", I need to know if there's a standard convention established. There isn't one yet.

However, I can speak to Mute to ask for more explicit information, assuming Mute can hear (which is implied by the role description not listing "Cannot Hear" for Mute). If Mute can hear, I can ask them to gesture a number or use a sequence.

- Wire 1 is Red.

- Wire 3 is Blue.

Blind gestures `👏 👏 👆 👆 👆`. Clapping might mean "Wait" or "Stop" or "Attention". Then 3 points.

Mute gestured `👎` (thumbs down) in response to my question "Does pointing up mean cut the first wire (red)?". This means **No**, pointing up does not mean cut the red wire.

Blind is now waving (`👋`) and then pointing up three times (`👆 👆 👆`). The wave might indicate "Stop" or "Hello/Attention", but combined with the previous clapping, it seems Blind is trying to communicate something about the number 3 or the third wire. This looks like an enumeration or a pattern.
If `👆` is not Red and not Blue, it might be Yellow? Or maybe `👆` isn't a wire selector but something else entirely.

Let's look at the Blind's sequence again:
1. `☝` (One)
2. `👆` (Up?)
3. `✌` (Two)
4. `👆` (Up?)
5. `🤟` (Three? The ILY gesture has 3 extended fingers)

It seems Blind is listing items 1, 2, 3... and pointing up after each? Or maybe `👆` means "Cut"?

Alternative interpretation:
Maybe the gestures from Mute are answers to Yes/No questions.
Q: Is it Red? A: No.
Q: Is it Blue? A: No.
So is it **Yellow**?

I will ask Mute: "Does pointing up mean cut the yellow wire?"


`✍` strongly suggests the **Plate**.
If Blind is pointing at the plate and then pointing up 3 times, maybe the instruction is related to the engraving on the plate.
